author: the_electrician
notes: Normal operation. All systems online. Kitchen, greenhouse, and water pump running simultaneously. Load within design parameters.

author: the_electrician
notes: Night cycle. Reduced load. Only essential systems: ventilation, cold storage, radio standby. Fuel consumption predictable.

author: the_electrician
notes: Water pump offline for 8 hours due to seal failure (see equip_failure_002). Load dropped during outage then spiked when pump restarted. Voltage dip noted. the_plumber seal repair resolved the issue.

author: the_electrician
notes: Radiation storm day. All ventilation at maximum. Air filter bank running continuously. Load at 80 percent for 14 hours. Voltage fluctuation within tolerance but concerning. Fuel consumption elevated.

author: the_electrician
notes: Post-storm normalisation. Blast door hydraulic failure required manual winch operation (see equip_failure_004). the_electrician began Variac bypass design during this downtime.

author: the_electrician
notes: Radio transmitter output reduced 40 percent due to amplifier tube degradation (see equip_failure_005). Reduced transmitter load saves approximately 0.5 litres fuel per day. Minor saving.

author: the_electrician
notes: Greenhouse grow light ballast failure affecting 2 of 6 banks (see equip_failure_006). Light load reduced. the_electrician rebuilt ballast with salvaged capacitors. Load restored to 68 percent.

author: the_electrician
notes: Stable day. All systems nominal. the_electrician used downtime to begin Variac bypass wiring. Parts sourced from salvage inventory.

author: the_electrician
notes: UV sterilisation lamp end-of-life (see equip_failure_009). Water treatment switched to chemical method. No significant power change. the_electrician monitoring hypochlorite supply.

author: the_electrician
notes: CRITICAL: Voltage regulator failed. Output spiked to 260V. the_electrician manually disconnected load within 30 seconds. No equipment damage. Variac bypass installed as permanent fix. 12 hours downtime. See equip_failure_010.

author: the_electrician
notes: Variac bypass operational. Voltage control is manual but stable. the_electrician must adjust during load changes. Fuel consumption down 8 percent from pre-failure baseline. The bypass is working.

author: the_electrician
notes: Stable operation under Variac control. the_electrician has developed a load-change protocol: adjust voltage before switching large loads. This prevents the spikes that destroyed the regulator.

author: the_electrician
notes: Cold storage compressor running continuously due to refrigerant leak (see equip_failure_013). Elevated load. the_electrician monitoring compressor amperage for signs of motor stress.

author: the_electrician
notes: Cold storage compressor cycling normally after seal repair. Load returned to normal. Blast door winch cable replaced (see equip_failure_014). All critical systems operational.

author: the_electrician
notes: Radio antenna capacitor cleaned and sealed (see equip_failure_015). Reception improved. No power impact. Monthly fuel consumption trending at 210 litres. At current rate, fuel reserves at 43 days.

author: the_electrician
notes: Water pump float valve failure caused 200 litre water loss (see equip_failure_016). No power impact. the_electrician installed manual override on the valve. the_plumber monitoring.

author: the_electrician
notes: Generator fuel filter clogged. Engine running at 60 percent power (see equip_failure_017). Load reduced to match. Filter replaced. the_chemist fuel treatment added. Fuel consumption temporarily reduced during low-power operation.

author: the_electrician
notes: Ventilation baffle re-anchored (see equip_failure_018). No power impact. TEG output reduced to 1.2W (see equip_failure_019). TEG now supplements approximately 0.5 litres fuel savings per day. Marginal but real.

author: the_electrician
notes: TEG thermoelectric module replaced with last spare. Output restored to 2.8W. No more spare modules. TEG operating schedule reduced to 8 hours per day to extend module life.

author: the_electrician
notes: CRITICAL: Generator exhaust gasket failure. CO detected. Generator room evacuated for 2 hours (see equip_failure_020). Generator offline for 14 hours total. the_mechanic fabricated new gasket. CO monitors now permanently installed. Generator back online at reduced load during recovery.
